Quixotic

kwik-SOT-ik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Quixotic is unrealistic and impractical, especially in pursuit of idealistic goals.

His quixotic plan to open a bookstore in a town with no reliable internet and a shrinking population impressed everyone, even as they doubted it could survive.

Worked Example

The freshman senator's quixotic campaign promise to eliminate all traffic within the city in one term charmed voters, even though everyone knew it was impossible.

Quixotic describes a goal that's admirable in spirit -- idealistic, even noble -- but almost certainly doomed by reality.

How Quixotic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

idealistic

idealistic: guided by high or perfect standards, sometimes unrealistically

impractical

impractical: not sensible or workable in reality (a word you met earlier in this course)

Antonyms

pragmatic

pragmatic: dealing with things realistically and practically

realistic

realistic: having a sensible view of what's achievable

How Strong Is It? — hopeful → quixotic → delusional

hopeful vs. quixotic

hopeful vs. quixotic: Hopeful describes mild optimism, without necessarily being unrealistic the way quixotic can be.

delusional vs. quixotic

delusional vs. quixotic: Delusional describes a belief completely disconnected from reality, more extreme than merely quixotic.

Build the Word

The pieces

eponym — Quixote

eponym — Quixote: named after Don Quixote, the idealistic but impractical knight from Cervantes' novel (Spanish, from the novel Don Quixote de la Mancha (1605))

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: characteristic of (Greek/Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Quixotic isn't built from a Latin or Greek root at all -- it comes straight from Don Quixote, the hero of Cervantes' novel who charged at windmills believing they were giants. A quixotic plan is one pursued with Don Quixote's noble but hopelessly unrealistic idealism.

Use the root in a new word: Don Quixote

Use the root in a new word: Don Quixote: In the novel, Don Quixote sets off on horseback to revive chivalry, mistaking ordinary windmills for fearsome giants.
